Act of February 21, 1863, ch. 53, 12 Stat. 658-660, read on govinfo: removal of the Winnebago from Minnesota, appraisal and sale of 'said reservation', debt lands sold under Article 3 of this treaty; no consent provision. The quote is exact.

The Act qualifies as an Act-of-Congress breach of THIS treaty: it removed the people from and sold the reservation this treaty's Article 1 set apart and retained. The Article 1 phrase 'until otherwise provided for by Congress' covers taxation, levy, sale or forfeiture of individual assigned tracts and does not reserve power to remove the tribe; recorded in openQuestions.
ICC Dockets 243-245 compromise (ids 1872, 2308): $4,600,000, covering Royce Areas 416 (sold under this treaty) and 439 (sold under the 1863 Act); correctly kind litigation.
Act of July 15, 1870, sec. 9, 16 Stat. 361: Secretary to investigate claims of Winnebago lawfully residing in Minnesota and issue patents for unsold allotted lands. Matches today.
